title: Fix WSGI Server Crash on Malformed/TLS Requests

1784355123.4023643.instruction: Read webcms/core/application.py, webcms/core/request.py, and any server entry points to understand how the WSGI server is started and how requests are processed. Identify where connection handling occurs and where we can add resilience.

1784355125.5977619.instruction: Create a custom WSGIRequestHandler subclass that wraps request handling in try/except to catch ConnectionResetError, OSError, and other socket errors silently. Override handle(), parse_request(), and handle_one_request() to prevent crashes from malformed requests and connection resets. Log at debug level instead of printing full tracebacks.

1784355128.0588076.instruction: Modify Application.run() in webcms/core/application.py to use the custom WSGIRequestHandler and a custom WSGIServer class that handles connection resets gracefully. Ensure the development server remains compatible with the existing API but resilient to malformed requests.

1784355130.8077407.instruction: Create middleware that validates incoming requests early in the pipeline: reject null bytes, control characters, invalid HTTP versions, and HTTP/2 PRI requests. Return 400 Bad Request for malformed requests before they reach application logic. This provides defense in depth even when the WSGI server accepts the connection.

1784355133.27105.instruction: Review webcms/core/request.py to ensure it handles edge cases safely: empty bodies, oversized content-length, invalid content-length values, malformed JSON, and invalid UTF-8. Add input validation to prevent exceptions from propagating and crashing the server.

1784355136.3121703.instruction: Create a simple test script that sends malformed requests (TLS bytes, connection reset, oversized request line, HTTP/2 PRI, null bytes) to the running server and verify it does not crash. Document the expected behavior: server should return 400 or silently close connection, and continue accepting new requests.
